claim_class: minimum preservation plus retained-coordinate optimizer projection and strict improvement (RPA 10): 3 directional claims (forward NonIncreasing with no projection; reverse Equal with 37,616 retained-coordinate pairs; conditional Equal projection under a caller-bound input halfspace) + 1 caller-bound strict improvement
claims: 1. Every source-MI feasible point maps to a complete target-MI point with nonincreasing objective (reverse=false, objective=NonIncreasing, projection=[]).
2. Every target-MI feasible point lifts to a complete source-MI point with equal objective and all 37,616 retained coordinates preserved (reverse=true, objective=Equal, projection has 37,616 pairs).

3. On the caller-bound original-source halfspace P<=0, where P is exactly the sum of all 200 original nonnegative continuous terminals, the source-MI point projects to a complete target-MI point with equal objective and every retained coordinate unchanged (reverse=false, objective=Equal, projection 37,616 pairs, input_halfspace = 200 terms, constant 0).
4. Whenever P>0, a complete source-MI point has a complete source-MI strict improvement (target=false, integers=true, positive predicate = P).
proof_encoding: Single RPA 10 certificate merged by byte splice from four separately authored and separately verified parts (forward, reverse, projection, improvement); the merged file is 267,140,625 B against the unchanged 268,435,456 B text limit and assembles to a 177,165,284 B RPX.

Two canonical chain roots (forward and improvement) each build the chain tuple with 19 SignedLift batches of ten prefix levels - 38 SignedLift steps total, 37,616 decompositions per root, each decomposition contributing 4 author-signed variables and 4 rows (300,928 generated variables / rows overall).

Terminal-sum Split at each root: inactive branch = Return / ImproveReturn with the constant 6,425 witness map plus per-variable bound and integrality checks and per-row checks; positive branch = guard assumption plus the 2,433 lower bound (195 binary contribution + 2,238 layer bound) and the constant 858 margin, or the 4,850-per-unit predicate margin for the improvement.

Each canonical coordinate is related to its original continuous counterpart by EqPair plus local Cases/Witness on the generated sign binary; anchors at every tenth prefix level and all 200 terminals additionally receive VarInt facts; every original chain row is re-derived through those sign facts.

Projection claim: exactly one appended caller row (200 terms, P<=0), P=0 by EqPair of its RowUpper against -sum(terminals)<=0 from actual VarLower bounds, each terminal<=0 by a balanced binary split recursion, the 200 changed target rows rebuilt by adding the matching terminal upper bound, the objective difference proved exactly -4,850*P, and 37,616 retained-identity checks emitted; the reverse claim emits the same 37,616 identities.
1,087,916 generated signed terms, 11,418,684 linear terms, 157,666 branches, 529,636 obligations, 448,596,660 work, 276,367 peak live facts.

The attack harness is re-implemented per case with lambdas and positional indices (e.g. remove(checks, 38216+20000) or checks index 2 inside a SignedLift decomposition), so each mutation is bound to an index into a 529,636-element obligation list.

Attempt preservation is manual duplication: pre-projection-completion/ duplicates a 250.4 MB RPA, its scripts, request and eight attacks; first-verbose-forward/ duplicates a 148,361,460-byte RPA, because there is no representation/partial-verification bookkeeping.

Certificate numbers that the domain agent derived (layer frequencies, five largest incidence counts, the 6,425 witness) are recomputed from scratch in the preparer (inspect, lower_base) and enter the proof as indices and constants; only the resulting linear facts are kernel-checked.

api_needs.why: The entire 267 MB certificate is hand-written step JSON: there is no public constructor (crates/core/src/build_support.rs is crate-private and trusted builders live only in crates/core/tests/*_builder.rs), so tools/prepare_test36_full.py imports a hand-rolled Proof step builder and adds case-specific inference writers. The chain/canonical-tuple construction is the load-bearing part: canonical_root builds 19 batches of ten prefix levels over 200 chains (longest prefix 191), decides which coordinates need integer facts (every anchor parent at a tenth level plus all 200 terminals), emits per item a flow expression, a capacity bound pair, the old row fact and an optional VarInt, then emits a local Cases with Witness branches per generated sign binary to prove each canonical coordinate equals its original continuous counterpart and to rewire every original chain row. Result: 38 SignedLift steps, 157,666 branches, 300,928 generated signed variables and rows, each SignedLift item hand-written as 4 generated variables + 4 rows.

notes: Scale for design purposes: 37,816 source vars / 37,617 rows / 113,048 nonzeros / 200 binaries; 529,636 obligations; 448,596,660 work; 157,666 branches; peak live facts 276,367; RPA 267,140,625 B (99.5% of the 268,435,456 B text limit); RPX 177,165,284 B; request.json 1,014,101 B. test36 is the extreme of the corpus: only case with input_halfspace / halfspace_domains>0, only case with RPA > 100 MB, only case with 38 SignedLift stages (next: test46 with 551,077,751 work / 1,105,551 obligations, the only other case that byte-splices parts). Preserved attempts (pre-projection-completion/ 250.4 MB RPA, first-verbose-forward/ 148,361,460 B RPA, attempts/ with the positive-terminal control point at objective 6,426) show that the compiler must support superseded plans and representation rewrites, not only incremental edits. The improvement proof's 6,425 witness and the 2,238 layer frequencies come from the domain agent's own chain reconstruction and enter the certificate as constants/indices; per cases/test36/README.md the kernel recomputes and proves the layer inequalities from actual rows, so the compiler mainly needs to carry author-side structural facts into the proof consistently.
